Week 80 Appendix: Consolidation Through Ordinary Machinery

This week the administration relied not on dramatic overreach but on tariffs, reclassifications, and appointments to entrench power while courts and senators pushed back.

This week combined an active foreign war with domestic institutional erosion across historic preservation, tariff authority, election administration, and law-enforcement accountability. The administration pursued a third consecutive workaround (Section 301/122 tariffs) after a Supreme Court defeat, continued reclassifying Iran-war casualties to dodge War Powers Act deadlines, and pushed a systematic campaign against the Smithsonian and historic-preservation law using an unqualified ideological advisor. Simultaneously, Senate Republicans stalled Trump's AG nominee over a $1.8 billion 'anti-weaponization' fund tied to Trump's own tax immunity, exposing intra-party friction even as Trump signaled he would bypass confirmation via indefinite 'acting' authority. ICE expanded enforcement into new populations (TPS Haitians, airport visa-expiration arrests, ORR data-sharing) while documented vetting and use-of-force failures went unaddressed. Media disinformation around Mamdani's 9/11 attendance revealed a self-reinforcing right-wing media ecosystem. Polling showed cratering approval amid economic strain from the war.

(2026-07-25)
  2. Trump rejected U.S. intelligence on Russian assistance to Iran in favor of Putin's personal denial: The president publicly discounted credible intelligence findings in favor of assurances from an adversarial foreign leader, raising questions about evidence-based national security decisions. (2026-07-25)

White House signed executive order directing warning signs at the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History: The order used executive power to discredit and pressure a federal cultural institution, asserting a single ideological narrative over independent historical scholarship.
